memory_candidates.content: scripts/check-module-invariants.sh's C5 (markdown module-path resolution) and C15 second assertion (theorem-index Paper:-anchor resolution) both read a declaration's fully-qualified Lean name with ASCII-only regexes. C5's dotted-segment matcher only recognizes consecutive Capitalized ASCII segments, so a namespace that deliberately does not mirror its directory nesting (e.g. `PlusSlicedCertificate.NoFiniteWidth` for a file at `PlusSlicedCertificate/Limits/NoFiniteWidth.lean`) needs an entry in the separate, sanctioned `scripts/module-invariants-allowlist.txt` data file -- editable even when the script itself is out of a task's file_scope, with existing precedent (e.g. `PlusSharingWitnessFamily`) documenting the exact exemption shape to copy. C15's second assertion's declaration-matching regex `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.']*` is ASCII-only and truncates any declaration name at its first non-ASCII character, so a theorem named with a trailing Greek letter (e.g. `not_plusValidZTime_neg_Φ`) can never be anchored by that check, structurally, regardless of docstring content -- a pre-existing checker limitation to report as a reasoned exclusion rather than treat as a defect in the landed theorem.

When narrowing a transcribed probe's `import FormalSystem` down to a minimal import list, `ring` is NOT transitively available just because other Semantics/Metalogic modules are imported -- it requires an explicit `import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring`, discoverable only by building (the probe's whole-library import masked this dependency). Separately, when trimming genuinely-unused `variable`-introduced section parameters from an internal (non-headline) declaration via `omit [...] in` to satisfy a zero-warning linter gate, every in-file positional call site of that declaration must be updated to drop the same parameters in the same call -- the trim is not local to the declaration's own body, because `omit` changes the declaration's actual parameter list, not just its warning status. This can cascade through a whole call chain (e.g. one inner helper's trim forces the same trim on every caller that only forwarded the now-unused parameter).
